messages.subject: camtrapR version 0.99.7 released
parts:
The new version of camtrapR (0.99.7) was released on CRAN.

Here's the news section of the new release:


Changes in camtrapR 0.99.7
==========================

bugfixes
------------
 o recordTable: returned station ID as camera ID if IDfrom = "metadata" and cameraID = "directory"
 
new features
------------
  o detectionMaps: gained argument 'backgroundPolgygon' for plotting a SpatialPolygon object in the background of the maps
  o imageRename: new argument 'createEmptyDirectories' to control whether empty directories should be copied or not
  o imageRename: if outDir contains images already, the function will not stop with an error, but asks you whether or not to copy new images (useful if data come in over time)
 
other changes
------------
  o recordTable / recordTableIndividual: improved handling and reporting of stations without images (warning instead of error)
  o recordTable / recordTableIndividual: improved handling and reporting of stations where all images lack species/individual metadata tags (only if using metadata ID, functions will throw warning instead of error)


There's also a new section about a possible issue with time zones and daylight saving time in vignette Date Extraction:
https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/camtrapR/vignettes/DataExtraction.html

In short: if you specify a time zone with daylight saving time, but your cameras don't record the time zone (and therefore don't use daylight saving time), records during DST will be off by 1 hour. In that case it's better to use the default UTC time zone.

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: camtrapR version 0.99.7 released
parts:
Dear Christy,
if you tag images in digiKam, these tags will be extracted and tabulated automatically by the function recordTable (and recordTableIndividual too). Assigning these tags is identical to species tagging. For example, create a tag group for Sex, and in it create 3 tags (male, female, unknown). The same goes for age class or other tags you may wish to assign.

Currently, I have no plans to include MCP plots in the package. That said, you can create them easily with the plotMCP function of the secr package. You need a capthist object, which is returned by spatialDetectionHistory.
See:
library(secr)
?plotMCP
example(plotMCP)

Regards,
Jürgen
